title: How an Induction Cooktop Works in 60 Seconds 🍳🧲 #shorts
description:
An induction cooktop never gets red hot, yet it boils water fast. A copper coil under the glass carries alternating current and makes a changing magnetic field. That field drives tiny electric currents inside a magnetic pan, and the pan heats itself. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#induction #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: This stove has no flame and no red-hot coil. The *pan* heats itself.

steps.label: Copper Coil
steps.text: Under the glass sits a flat *copper coil*. Alternating current rushes through it.

steps.label: Magnetic Field
steps.text: The current builds a *magnetic field* that flips back and forth, thousands of times a second.

steps.label: Tiny Currents
steps.text: That changing field drives small *electric currents* inside the metal of the pan.

steps.label: Heat
steps.text: The pan's metal resists those currents, and that resistance becomes *heat*.

steps.label: Magnetic Pans
steps.text: It only works with *magnetic* pans. Aluminum or glass alone stays cold.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Coil, field, currents, *heat*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
